title: X509Chain and PEM export
summary: Configure X509ChainPolicy precisely, read ChainElements and ChainStatus, and export a full chain as PEM.

steps.title: X509ChainPolicy, setting by setting
body: p.TrustMode = X509ChainTrustMode.CustomRootTrust;   // trust ONLY CustomTrustStore, not the OS roots
p.ExtraStore.Add(intermediate);                     // candidates, like the certs a server sends
p.RevocationMode = X509RevocationMode.NoCheck;      // Online in production; NoCheck for offline tests
p.VerificationTime = new DateTime(2031, 6, 1, 0, 0, 0, DateTimeKind.Utc);  // "now" for date checks
foreach (X509ChainElement e in chain.ChainElements)      // leaf first, anchor last
foreach (X509ChainStatus s in chain.ChainStatus)          // overall problems
`VerificationTime` defaults to *now*, which makes tests time bombs. Set it. Each element also has its own `ChainElementStatus`
if you need to know *which* certificate failed.

steps.prompt: Match each policy setting to what it controls.
pairs: the certificates that end a chain successfully
extra certificates the builder may use as intermediates
the moment validity dates are checked against
the EKU purposes the leaf must allow

steps.prompt: Complete the policy: trust only `root`, allow `inter` as an intermediate, and require server authentication.
steps.explain: `ApplicationPolicy` checks EKU; `CertificatePolicy` is about certificate policy OIDs, a different extension.

steps.prompt: Which certificate failed? `ChainElements` still lists every certificate found, even when `Build` returns false. Here the leaf expired in 2031. What does it print?
code: static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);
var inter = DojoCert("CN=Issuing CA", root, true);
var leaf = DojoCert("CN=old.example", inter, false, "old.example", null, 2030, 2031);
steps.explain: Per-element status pinpoints the culprit: only the leaf is out of date. `chain.ChainStatus` would just say `NotTimeValid` for the chain as a whole.

steps.prompt: A unit test that builds a chain passed for a year, then started failing on 1 January with `NotTimeValid`. Nobody changed the code. What's the best fix?
options: Set `ChainPolicy.VerificationTime` to a fixed date inside the test certificates' validity
Make the test certificates valid for 100 years
Catch the exception and mark the test inconclusive
steps.explain: Without `VerificationTime` the chain checks against the real clock. A fixed time makes the test deterministic forever.

steps.title: Report on a chain
prompt: Write `List<string> ChainReport(X509Certificate2 leaf, X509Certificate2 root, List<X509Certificate2> intermediates)` that builds
a chain (custom root trust, `intermediates` in `ExtraStore`, no revocation, serverAuth policy, verification time 2031-06-01 UTC)
and returns one line per element, leaf first:
For an element with problems, write its status flags joined by `,` instead of `ok`. When no path is found at all
(`PartialChain`), the chain still contains whatever elements were found, so just report those.
starter: List<string> ChainReport(X509Certificate2 leaf, X509Certificate2 root, List<X509Certificate2> intermediates)
solution: List<string> ChainReport(X509Certificate2 leaf, X509Certificate2 root, List<X509Certificate2> intermediates)
string status = e.ChainElementStatus.Length == 0 ? "ok" : string.Join(",", e.ChainElementStatus.Select(s => s.Status));
hints: Same policy setup as before; then loop over `chain.ChainElements`.
template: var dojoInter = DojoCert("CN=Issuing CA", dojoRoot, true);
var dojoClient = DojoCert("CN=device", dojoInter, false, null, "1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2");
Dojo.Eq("healthy chain", new List<string> { "CN=shop.example: ok", "CN=Issuing CA: ok", "CN=Root: ok" }, ChainReport(dojoLeaf, dojoRoot, new() { dojoInter }));
Dojo.Eq("clientAuth leaf", new List<string> { "CN=device: NotValidForUsage", "CN=Issuing CA: ok", "CN=Root: ok" }, ChainReport(dojoClient, dojoRoot, new() { dojoInter }));
Dojo.Eq("missing intermediate: only the leaf is found", 1, ChainReport(dojoLeaf, dojoRoot, new()).Count);
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);

steps.title: Exporting the full chain
body: Servers like nginx, and Kestrel's `CertificatePath` setting, want a **full chain PEM**: the leaf, then each intermediate,
and normally **not** the root. One `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----` block per certificate, one after another:
if (e.Certificate.Subject != e.Certificate.Issuer)        // skip the self-signed root
The private key goes in its own file with `key.ExportPkcs8PrivateKeyPem()` (protect it!), or the leaf plus key into a PFX with
To read a bundle back, `X509Certificate2Collection.ImportFromPem(text)` loads every block.

steps.title: Write fullchain.pem
prompt: Write `string FullChainPem(X509Certificate2 leaf, X509Certificate2 root, List<X509Certificate2> intermediates)`:
1. build the chain as before (custom root trust, no revocation, verification time 2031-06-01 UTC; no EKU policy needed),
3. otherwise return the PEM of every chain element **except the root**, in chain order, each followed by `\n`.
`ExportCertificatePem()` gives one block without a trailing newline.
starter: string FullChainPem(X509Certificate2 leaf, X509Certificate2 root, List<X509Certificate2> intermediates)
solution: string FullChainPem(X509Certificate2 leaf, X509Certificate2 root, List<X509Certificate2> intermediates)
if (!chain.Build(leaf)) throw new InvalidOperationException("chain does not validate");
hints: Skip the element whose Subject equals its Issuer.
Use `Append(...).Append('\n')` rather than `AppendLine`, which may add `\r\n` on Windows.
template: var dojoInter = DojoCert("CN=Issuing CA", dojoRoot, true);
var dojoPem = FullChainPem(dojoLeaf, dojoRoot, new() { dojoInter, dojoRoot });
Dojo.Eq("leaf first, then the intermediate", new List<string> { "CN=shop.example", "CN=Issuing CA" }, dojoBack.Cast<X509Certificate2>().Select(c => c.Subject).ToList());
Dojo.Check("ends with a newline", dojoPem.EndsWith("\n"), "add \\n after each block");
Dojo.Throws<InvalidOperationException>("throws when the chain is broken", () => FullChainPem(dojoLeaf, dojoRoot, new()));

req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
